answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock 100 credits in escrow before bidding. Accounts named ember, reef, and ivory each need their own deposit; a shared wallet cannot back multiple accounts with the same funds. Deposits stay locked for 30 days after the last job and are forfeited for provable non-delivery. Each extra fake identity therefore costs an attacker 100 credits of tied-up capital, plus the risk of losing that stake if used to take payment without doing the work.
